Forwarded from Mike — Island Time Electrical Details:

10 x 100Ah DragonFly Lithium batteries, professionally installed with copper bus bars. Having 10 separate batteries spreads heavy current loads across the bank and keeps it cooler.

Victron MultiPlus 3000/12/120 inverter/charger. The 3000W inverter supports more simultaneous appliances and the 120A charger allows quick charging from shore or generator. It also allows current limits to be set.

Victron BMV-712 battery monitor, SmartShunt, Color Control GX and VRM portal allow complete control and monitoring, including remotely over Starlink.

6 x 320W SunPower solar panels for 1,920W total. We ran the boat for three seasons with very little generator use — just a couple hundred hours over three years. Four panels feed a Victron 150/70 MPPT, two coachroof panels feed a Victron 100/50 MPPT, and a third 75/15 MPPT is installed as a spare.

The Frigomar A/C units use variable-speed brushless DC inverter compressors. They can pull about 1200W on startup but typically run 600–800W. A six-hour night-mode example works out to roughly 300Ah, about 30% of the 1,000Ah bank. With around 1,200W of solar output the next day, that 300Ah can be replaced in roughly 3.5–4 hours.

That's the simple explanation of how we set Island Time up to run off-grid. There are many variables, but we were balanced and ran for weeks at a time without the generator.
